canonical_title: No effect system for tracking side effects in function execution
canonical_definition: Families 8, 9, 10 show that algebraic effect handlers, probabilistic programming, and agent skill compilation all require explicit effect tracking. Ignition functions have no effect system.

direct_evidence.summary: S120-053 (Algebraic Effects, JLC 2009, VERIFIED) provides effect handlers separating effect signatures from interpreters.

analogical_evidence.summary: 121CX entries provide indirect support for agent skill effects.

negative_evidence.summary: Effect handlers are language-level, not tied to neural function execution. Agent skill systems lack formal effect calculus. No cross-representation effect tracking.

supported_claims: Algebraic effect handlers provide rigorous separation of effects from interpreters
Effect tracking is feasible for symbolic program execution
unsupported_claims: Effect handlers not tied to neural function execution
No formal effect calculus for agent skills
residual_gap: Strong theoretical foundation but requires integration into ignition's execution runtime. Most ignition functions are pure math with no side effects.
confidence_basis: MEDIUM. Strong theory (S120-053 VERIFIED) but limited applicability to ignition's mathematical functions.
recommended_next_action: Add effect_signature field to N1 (FunctionSpec). Most ignition functions will be 'pure'. Track effects only for agent-facing functions.
prohibited_wording: Do not claim 'ignition functions have proven side effects' or 'algebraic effects solve Function OS execution'.
